data.turoyo: Kul ḥəššabo kul tre gzayri i kalaṯṯe, <...>
data.translation: Jeden Sonntag oder jeden zweiten Sonntag besuchen sie ihre (künftige) Schwiegertochter, <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; periodic visits with zero-marked feminine human object.

data.turoyo: Gaban kit ʕade: kuhno rabo i naqqa d kzoyər, ḥa bəlxašša b yawme dam marasəm, kmitəstaqbəl u kuhno, ḥasyo aw faṭəryarxo baq qole.
data.translation: Es ist bei uns Sitte, daß, wenn ein hoher Priester jemanden besonders bei feierlichen Gelegenheiten besucht, man ihn, sei er Priester, Metropolit oder Patriarch, mit geistlichen Liedern empfangt.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; customary visit with indefinite human object ḥa.

data.turoyo: Bi dʕərto d daʕirina l Məḏyaḏ fayitina l Zaz i qriṯo. Zərlan u qadišo Mor Diməṭ.
data.translation: Auf der Rückfahrt nach Midyat kamen wir durch das dorf Zaz. Dort besuchten wir Mor Dimit.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; first-person plural visitors and overt visited saint/sanctuary.

data.turoyo: I ʕuǧubaṯe hawyo sabab li zəyara du ʕulmo mhayəmno.
data.translation: Dieses Wunder wurde die Ursache für den Besuch des gläubigen Volkes.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv cell; genitive identifies the visiting people, unlike the existing possessive for those visited.

data.turoyo: Hiya ste aṯyo li zəyara du qadišano w maʕmallala quṣro ǧiran di ʕito, m traḥṣar qaṭat.
data.translation: Auch sie kam, das Heiligtum zu besuchen, und baute sich ein zwölfstöckiges Schloß in der Nachbarschaft der Kirche.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv cell; genitive visited holy referent, retained without deciding person versus sanctuary.

data.turoyo: Ḥasyo Ḥanna aṯiwo l gabayna li zyara.
data.translation: Der Metropolit Ḥanna von Mardin war zu uns auf Besuch gekommen.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv cell; purpose noun without a possessive participant.

data.turoyo: Ḥaqiqatan ġalabe abəʕno d əzzino li zyarayḏe.
data.translation: Ich wollte ihm tatsächlich gern meine Aufwartung machen.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv cell to five; third-person visited participant encoded by possessive suffix; this clause has a matching edition translation.

summary: Finite visiting takes zero-marked human or place objects and pronominal object suffixes. No Detransitive, new stem or special prepositional sense is established.

Infinitiv zyara/ziyara is retained in the glossary's existing category. Genitive/possessive participants can be visitors (11/111) or visited people (19/2; 68/6), with interpretation supplied by syntax and context rather than one fixed possessive role.
The nominal visitors zayore is already in Part act.; do not infer a separate finite form or new sense.

Repeated add/thin_cell proposals for an already quoted citation, especially 19/2, are deduplicated. The selected 68/6 sentence has a matching translation despite omissions elsewhere in the supplied full verse.
Does u qadišano at 11/113 denote the holy man or the sacred site? The edition chooses Heiligtum.
In 68/57, does the genitive ruler denote the visitor to Diyarbekir or the person whom the priest visited? The German resolves it more specifically than the Turoyo alone.
Can editors confirm whether zyara is best retained as the glossary's Infinitiv or separately indexed as the borrowed event noun? No category change is proposed here.
Visited referents include people, places and saint/sanctuary designations; the same visit meaning applies.
